Tip Text: Reporting whether or not snow is present on the ground or treetops is useful to scientists who use satellite images to study plant cover. Since sunlight reflected off snow can look the same as bright green leaves in these images, your reports can eliminate some of the guesswork in interpreting satellite images. By comparing the ground observations you take at your site to a satellite image of the area that includes your site, these scientists can "ground truth" or "validate" the images, and therefore become better at interpreting other images across the globe.

Sync Over Wi-Fi Only - With this setting enabled, Nature's Notebook will only attempt to send data back to the NPN when the phone is actively connected to  Wi-Fi. This is useful if you have a low bandwidth phone plan or you spend a lot of time recording data in remote places without a connection. This is enabled by default.

Include Time in Dates Observed - With this setting enabled, you can recod the time of day in addition to the date, when making observations. This is useful if you observe a lot of animals and want to capture the exact time of day. This is disabled by default.
